Monday 23 November 2026 · 22 stories
Morning Brief
Nifty 50 rose 1.12% to 25,801 but decliners led 1,695 to 867
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +2.06% weighted by turnover, against -0.73% for the median stock, a gap of 2.8 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Ugro Capital Limited rose 9.6% on 444 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about fund raising, “Allotment of 105000 securities (NCDs) pursuant to Non Convertible Securities at its meeting held on November 19, 2026”.

Tips Films Limited rose 6.2% on 106 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Zee Entertain Share Price, Zee Entertain Stock Price, Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd. Stock Price, Share Price, Live BSE/NSE, Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd. Bids Offers. Buy/Sell Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd. news & tips, & F&O Quotes, NSE/BSE”.

Jupiter Life Line Hospitals Limited rose 12.9% on 183 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Why British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh risked his life in war-hit Strait of Hormuz”.

Nothing in the news or in exchange filings explains the volume in Oriental Aromatics Limited (111x), V2 Retail Limited (73x), HMA Agro Industries Limited (70x). That usually points to a sector story rather than a company one.

What happened
Breaking
Dollar edges off 19-month high after market rout; yen softens
The US Dollar Index pulled back slightly after touching a 19-month high during a global market sell-off. A stronger dollar weakens the rupee, encouraging foreign portfolio outflows from Indian equities and raising landed costs for imported commodities. This pause offers temporary relief to foreign institutional flows and margin pressures for crude-dependent sectors like paints and chemicals.
Reuters Business · +2 others
FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri International over unsafe packaged water - The Economic Times
Food regulator FSSAI sanctioned prosecution against unlisted Bisleri International after sample tests revealed unsafe packaged drinking water. While Bisleri is unlisted, tighter regulatory enforcement elevates compliance risk and audit scrutiny across listed beverage and FMCG players like Varun Beverages and Tata Consumer Products. Quality audit reports from state FDA branches in coming weeks will show if this compliance crackdown spreads.
Geopolitics
Gold Rebounds as Traders Pare Bets on Near-Term Fed Rate Hikes - Bloomberg.com
Gold prices rebounded as financial markets pared expectations for imminent Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. Lower US rate expectations support foreign fund flows into emerging market equities by narrowing yield differentials. Higher bullion prices also expand loan-to-value cushions for gold NBFCs like Muthoot Finance and support inventory gains for jewelers like Titan Company.

Nashik eyes data centre hub status after Mumbai, Pune - The Times of India
Nashik municipal authorities launched planning initiatives to position the city as Maharashtra's next data centre hub after Mumbai and Pune. Regional expansion of data infrastructure increases long-term power and construction capex, benefiting industrial equipment suppliers like ABB India and Siemens. Substation orders from Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company will confirm initial grid infrastructure spending in Nashik.

US seeks answers on Nvidia's sale of chips to China, Bessent says
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent launched an inquiry into how restricted Nvidia chips reached Chinese end-users through third-party intermediaries. Tighter US tech export controls increase compliance risks and cost overheads for global cloud providers. For Indian IT services majors like Infosys and TCS, any delay in AI hardware deployment by US enterprise clients threatens short-term AI deal conversion rates.
AI & data centresReuters Business
Going to be nuts! Elon Musk warns of massive AI cash crunch in 2027, asks ‘Where will that money come from?’
Elon Musk projected an industry-wide capital shortfall for global AI expansion by 2027 as data center construction and chip costs outpace available funding. A slowdown in hyperscaler capital expenditure would reduce global order inflows for Indian electrical equipment and cooling solution providers such as ABB India and Schneider Electric Infrastructure. Upcoming quarterly order commentary from capital goods firms will confirm if execution timelines are stretching.

Water Management Stock With Order Book 400% Higher Than Annual Revenue to Keep an Eye On - Trade Brains
A domestic water engineering company reported an unexecuted order backlog exceeding four times its annualized revenue. Strong order coverage provides revenue visibility for small-cap water treatment EPC companies like VA Tech Wabag. However, working capital constraints and municipal payment delays often cap cash flow conversion, making working capital cycle metrics in upcoming quarterly filings the critical operating metric to track.

Australia shares set to slide at open, NZ falls
Early-morning index movements in Australia and New Zealand reflect routine daily trading sentiment and carry no direct structural impact on Indian equity markets.

Correction or deeper reckoning? Investors seek signs US stock selling will abate
Broad selling in US equities accelerated as sticky inflation data pushed Treasury yields higher, dampening global equity valuation multiples. Persistent US market weakness suppresses foreign institutional portfolio inflows into India, placing downside pressure on the rupee and rich domestic valuations. Foreign institutional investor net selling figures over the next five trading sessions will indicate whether capital reallocation away from India is intensifying.

Macro and economy
COMMENTARY: AI bust hurts Chinese stocks far more than GDP
A sharp derating in Chinese artificial intelligence equities is pulling down regional tech valuations and prompting portfolio realignments across Asia. As foreign institutional investors trim high-beta Chinese technology holdings, capital typically rotates into defensive Indian large-cap financial and consumer stocks. Net foreign portfolio investment flows into Indian cash equities over the next three sessions will confirm whether this regional reallocation materializes.
Reuters Business
Stock market outlook today,23 Nov:Sensex, Nifty prediction-DJIA, S&P, NASDAQ, GIFT Nifty, Kospi, Nikkei, Taiwan cues
Indian equity benchmarks extended gains for a fourth consecutive week to hit nine-month highs, driven by large-cap banking stocks despite global technology sell-offs. Sustained banking performance protects net interest margins, but elevated domestic valuations face scrutiny ahead of the upcoming Reserve Bank of India policy meeting and economic growth data. The third-quarter GDP growth reading due this week will confirm whether underlying macroeconomic expansion supports current market multiples.
Mint Markets
Fed officials are chatting up a storm. Investors are in the dark about their plans.
Federal Reserve officials signaled divergent views on the magnitude of upcoming interest rate hikes intended to curb persistent inflation. Higher US interest rates widen the yield differential against Indian sovereign bonds, accelerating foreign portfolio outflows and weakening the rupee against the dollar. A depreciating rupee inflates input costs for net-importing sectors like chemicals and oil refining, while the upcoming US inflation print will clarify currency trajectory.
Mint Markets
Indian IT’s growth revival remains elusive despite better Q2
Indian IT service providers reported modest margin stability in second-quarter results, yet deal wins and revenue conversion rates remained stagnant across major verticals. Selective discretionary spending by North American financial clients delays top-line recovery for tier-one vendors like Infosys, TCS, and Wipro, leaving earnings growth dependent on cost cutting rather than volume expansion. Total contract value metrics in upcoming quarterly client updates will indicate whether discretionary IT budgets are unfreezing.
Mint Markets
Companies and earnings
Perfetti Van Melle to close 2026 at ₹4,000 crore revenue; tough year ahead, says MD
Perfetti Van Melle expects 2026 revenue to reach ₹4,000 crore, but warned that rising raw sugar and flexible packaging costs are squeezing gross margins. The unlisted confectionery giant is altering price-pack architecture and downsizing grammage to defend margins. Rising input costs signal margin headwinds for listed FMCG majors like Nestle India and Britannia Industries, which share similar unit economics at single-digit price points.
Mint Companies
Tata Steel to sell tubes business, Tata Steel Colors stake to APL Apollo for up to $3 billion
Tata Steel agreed to sell its structural tubes division and its stake in Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo Tubes for up to $3 billion. The transaction allows Tata Steel to reduce net debt and fund its Indian blast furnace expansions. For APL Apollo, the acquisition eliminates a major competitor and expands its market share in structural steel tubes past 60%, enhancing its pricing power.
Reuters Business
'Another mistake’: Bill Ackman joins Scott Bessent in warning US Fed against a rate cut in December | Hindustan Times - Hindustan Times
Prominent US investors are pushing back against a December Federal Reserve rate cut, citing stubborn service inflation. A paused Fed rate trajectory widens the US-India interest rate differential, keeping the US dollar strong against the rupee. Higher US yields limit the Reserve Bank of India's room to cut repo rates and dampen foreign portfolio flows into Indian equities.
Fed and rates
Geopolitics
COMMENTARY: China's steel sector bifurcates as iron ore remains robust
China’s steel sector is suffering margin compression as iron ore prices remain elevated despite weak domestic steel demand. High input costs in China prevent global steel prices from falling sharply, but cheap Chinese steel exports continue to cap Indian domestic steel realizations. Integrated Indian miners like NMDC benefit from firm ore pricing, whereas non-integrated steel producers face margin pressure.
Reuters Business
Defence tech funding cools after Operation Sindoor gold rush
Venture funding for Indian defence technology startups fell to $73 million in 2026 from $304 million in 2025 as long public procurement cycles delayed revenue realization. The capital slowdown reduces competitive disruption for incumbent listed defence equipment makers such as Bharat Electronics and Data Patterns. These cash-rich listed suppliers may find attractive acquisition targets among capital-starved startups to bolster their internal research capabilities.
Mint Companies
India's software services exports boom leaves IT companies behind
India’s total technology exports reached $264.4 billion in FY26 from $233.3 billion in FY25, driven by corporate Global Capability Centres rather than third-party IT vendors. Multinationals are insourcing tech operations into captive Indian units, directly cannibalizing revenue growth for listed majors like TCS, Infosys, and Wipro. Upcoming quarterly filings will confirm if client headcount reductions at listed IT firms are accelerating.
